processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding for 120 s at 1200 °C.
Cooled to the set deformation temperature T (1000 °C for this sample) at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (1000 °C) before compression so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant strain rate compression performed at T = 1000 °C and strain rate ε̇ = 10 s^-1 to a maximum compression of 60% (true strain 0.92). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down immediately.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (as-forged) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch used for this sample: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries, with dark grey grain interiors containing many fine, closely spaced parallel light-grey striations/lamellae (dendritic/interdendritic segregation banding); a few grains are almost featureless. The grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar.

After 60% hot compression (true strain 0.92) at 1000 °C / 10 s^-1 the steel has undergone dynamic recrystallization (DRX). The degree of DRX increases in the order difficult deformation zone (1) < small deformation zone (2) < large deformation zone (3). At high strain rate (10 s^-1) the DRX grains nucleate as small, equiaxed necklace grains distributed along the elongated original grain boundaries. DRX extent increases with increasing temperature and with decreasing strain rate, but the recrystallized grain size increases accordingly. No sample-specific optical micrograph is reported for the exact 1000 °C/10 s^-1 condition (Fig. 9 panels are given for 1100 °C controls and for 950, 1050 and 1150 °C at 1 s^-1).

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (3), core of the compressed specimen (grain size measured from the core)

defects.type: dislocation substructure (elongated original grains, work hardening)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: heterogeneous; high strain rate gives small but insufficient DRX grains with remnant large original grains

characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing (thermo-mechanical simulation)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C, ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1, cylindrical specimen F 8 mm × 12 mm, maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92), mica foils with high-temperature lubricants on end faces
characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain rheological (flow) stress curves and study hot deformation and dynamic recrystallization behavior
characterization_methods.key_findings: Steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material; peak/characteristic stress-strain values were derived from these curves.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, prepared, ground, polished and etched with 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.purpose: Collect microstructure images of the deformed specimen in the three deformation zones and measure DRX grain size in the large deformation zone (core)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Degree of DRX: large deformation zone > small deformation zone > difficult deformation zone; DRX grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature.

computational_details.simulation_method: Constitutive analysis using the Arrhenius hyperbolic sine function equation and the Zener-Hollomon parameter (multiple linear regression)
computational_details.software_used: linear regression (Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm used for grain-size model regression)
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Deformation conditions T = 900–1150 °C (converted to K) and ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1, peak stress σp
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Slopes k1 = 5.135 (ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)]) and k2 = 15.690 (ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T) from linear fits of experimental flow-stress data (Fig. 4); fitted lines not perfectly parallel, so Qp is an average value over the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate strain rate, peak stress and temperature to determine the dynamic recrystallization activation energy

parameters.name: k1 (average slope, ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)])

analytical_models.model_note: Equation: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n exp(-Qp/RT); Qp computed from Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2. Model is alloy-level (derived from the full T/ε̇ matrix that includes this sample).

analytical_models.equation_role: Group temperature and strain-rate effect on flow stress into one dimensionless parameter: Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT)
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ increases with strain rate or decreasing temperature; value for this sample taken from Table 1.

computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation and Poliak-Jonas inflection-point analysis
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Flow stress curves under different T and ε̇
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: C fitted from ln(σ/σp) vs [ln(ε/εp)+1-ε/εp]; at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 C = 0.1461 with R = 0.9728

analytical_models.model_name: Cingara-McQueen equation (Eq. 4) with work-hardening rate (Eq. 6) and critical strain expression (Eq. 9)
analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the critical strain for the onset of dynamic recrystallization
analytical_models.model_note: Equation: σ/σp = [ (ε/εp) exp(1-ε/εp) ]^C; εc/εp = [ (√(1-C) - (1-C)) / C ] ≈ 0.452, consistent with literature for low-density high-strength steel.

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression of characteristic flow-stress values against lnZ
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: lnZ values (Table 1) and corresponding critical/peak/steady-state stress-strain values
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Regression correlation coefficients R: σc 0.947, εc 0.911, σp 0.957, εp 0.911, σs 0.956, εs 0.922

analytical_models.equation_role: Express critical, peak and steady-state strains/stresses as functions of lnZ
analytical_models.model_note: Alloy-level models derived across all T and ε̇ conditions; used to build the DRX state diagram (regions A work hardening, B partial DRX, C complete DRX).

computational_details.simulation_method: Regression of DRX average grain size (Levenberg-Marquardt optimization) and finite element modelling
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D finite element software; Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as rigid plastic body, die indenter as rigid body, semi-symmetric specimen model; interface friction set to shear type with value 0.3; billet-air convection coefficient 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); initial grain size and strain taken as fixed values
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted vs experimental DRX grain size: correlation coefficient R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 µm

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model (Eq. 12)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict DRX average grain size from strain rate and temperature

parameters.name: a (constant, incl. d0 and strain terms)

analytical_models.model_note: Equation: d_rex = 807743.63 ε̇^-0.1903 exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338. General form (Eq. 11): d_rex = a d0^h ε^p ε̇^q exp(Q/RT) + b. Alloy-level model applicable to this sample's hot deformation.

unmapped_findings: For this sample's exact deformation condition (T = 1000 °C, ε̇ = 10 s^-1) the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 65.59 (Table 1).

No numeric peak stress (σp), characteristic strain/stress values, or DRX average grain size is printed in the text for the exact 1000 °C/10 s^-1 condition; the flow-stress and grain-size data for this condition are shown only graphically (Fig. 3, Fig. 10, Fig. 11), while explicit numeric values are given only for 900 °C and 1150 °C at 0.01 and 10 s^-1 (e.g. peak stress falls from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C at 0.01 s^-1, an 82% reduction; at 10 s^-1 the peak stress falls by 73% over the same temperature range).
The steel exhibits negative temperature sensitivity and positive strain-rate sensitivity: rheological stress (and peak stress) increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature.

The paper recommends a hot-working window for fine, uniform DRX grains of 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1; the sample condition of 1000 °C/10 s^-1 lies at the intersection of a mid temperature and the highest strain rate and is not inside the recommended windows.

The DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 the grain size exceeds 70 µm (coarse grains), whereas at low temperature (900–950 °C) and high strain rate (1–10 s^-1) DRX grains are small but incomplete with large remnant original grains.
Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (alloy-level, average over the experimental range).

The experimental phenomena (bulk composition, compression behavior, microstructure and reproducibility) were confirmed reproducible using the same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch under identical experimental conditions.
